# ARC Grid Reasoning

Use for ARC-style visual/grid transformation tasks, including streams where tasks recur with fresh inputs.

## Recurring task-d2414d9a caution and this failed instance
Task d2414d9a remains unresolved. Across recurring examples, uniform background cells are selectively recolored to the embedded marker color; selection is nontrivial and NOT ordinary flood fill. In this instance we used all 8 demos and failed all 8 submissions. Test grid 22x17, background 0, marker 5 cluster near lower-right (rows 15-18, cols 13-15), distractor foreground 6. Demos (summaries):
- Pair 1, 13x26, bg4, marker5. Marker forms small irregular object around r2-6,c8-10. Output selectively recolors many 4 cells to 5 throughout grid, notably scattered regions, while leaving many similar 4 cells unchanged.
- Pair 2, 16x13,bg2,marker8: short vertical/diagonal seed near upper-right; many selected 2s changed to 8, scattered across rows 1-13, while most 2s unchanged.
- Pair 3,19x19,bg9,marker8: several marker seeds around r10-12,c7-9; many 9s changed to 8 across broad regions; most other 9s remain.
- Pair 4,18x22,bg8,marker6: seed at r1-3,c3-9, output selectively recolors 8s to 6 scattered across grid, concentrated in lower/left and some middle areas.
- Pair 5,24x10,bg0,marker2 vertical line at r2-4,c5: many 0s selectively become 2, with dense broad regions in left columns early and varying positions elsewhere; 6s and most zeros preserved.
- Pair 6,13x14,bg5,marker7: seed around r6-9,c4-8; only a small region to right/top around r4-7,c10-13 changes from 5 to 7, leaving most background unchanged.
- Pair 7,12x27,bg4,marker3: seed near upper-left (r0-2,c4-5); extensive but selective 4→3 changes broadly throughout grid, with conspicuous large untouched 4 regions.
- Pair 8,23x12,bg2,marker6: seed near r12-14,c6-8; selective 2→6 changes across upper rows and near seed/bottom, most cells unchanged.
Failed candidate families on this test: global recolor; 4-neighbor flood fill; 8-neighbor flood fill; 0-components adjacent to seed; local 3x3/8-neighbor dilation; row/column projections from seed; identity/preserve seed only. All rejected. Do not repeat these. Need derive exact geometric/relational selection using all demo changed-cell masks; likely structured relation beyond connectivity, not enough evidence here. Always compare all changed and unchanged cells; don't extrapolate from proximity or component connectivity alone.

## Recurring task-197199f9: 3x3 downsample by non-background majority
Partition into aligned 3x3 blocks; output the modal non-background color per block, ignoring the uniform canvas/background color. If a block contains only background, output background. Confirmed by two demos (18x18→6x6 and 24x24→8x8) and accepted multiple tests, including 12x12→4x4. Partition into aligned 3x3 blocks; output the modal non-background color per block, ignoring uniform canvas/background (if no foreground, output background). Only selected row-runs of 7 were extended to the right edge by recoloring the remaining cells in that row to 1: in the first example, rows 6 and 7 (0-indexed) had foreground 7 reaching to col 20, then cols 21-22 became 1. Other bars/runs remained unchanged, so selection is not simply every row containing 7; the exact selector remains uncertain. A second demo (background 0, bar color 5) showed 1 replacing only the zero-valued suffix after a bar: row 0 cols16-18; row 7 cols13-18; row 10 cols8-18. Thus extend the marked horizontal bar to the right edge for rows with an incomplete bar, changing cells after its right endpoint to 1; completed runs reaching the edge remain unchanged. On the test, the bar on row 10 (0-indexed) has 6 through col20 and background 0 in cols21-25, so recolor those five suffix cells to 1. Preserve all other rows/cells. Confirmed correct on task-648a8222 test (22x26, background 0, bar color 6).

## Recurring task-11bc55ea: shift foreground down one row
The transform is a one-row downward translation of the entire grid pattern, preserving background and foreground values and clipping the bottom row. The top row becomes background. This is repeatedly demo-confirmed: pair 1 shifted sparse 9s down (2x10); pair 2 shifted an irregular 8 shape down (9x7); pair 3 shifted an irregular 0 pattern down (9x22); pair 4 shifted 9 pattern down (3x14); pair 6 shifted 9 region down (23x17); pair 7 shifted dense 1-field down (19x30); pair 8 shifted 2 block down (4x14). Pair 5 is an identity input-output pair, so does not contradict the rule. Multiple tests accepted, including backgrounds 4/3/2. Earlier accepted examples include 15x30 bg4/fg8 and 29x27 bg3/fg9. Critical pitfall: reliably transcribe the entire test grid and mechanically shift rows; manual row transcription errors caused several rejected submissions despite the right rule. Build each output row as the exact preceding input row, plus a fresh background row at top; check H×W dimensions and row lengths programmatically. Bottom source row is clipped.

## Recurring task-648a8222 accepted test update
An instance was accepted with zero wrong attempts: 22x25 background 0, full-width color-9 bar on row 8, and partial color-9 bar on row 16 spanning cols 0-19. Change only row 16's suffix cols 20-24 to color 1; preserve the full-width row and all other cells. This confirms selected-bar right-suffix completion, but does not reveal the selection criterion across varying task layouts. A prior second-demo summary suggests some examples select multiple incomplete bars, so do not assume universally “only lowest” or “every incomplete bar”; use examples to resolve selection.

## Workflow
1. Parse dimensions, background, all non-background cells, and motifs; track coordinates consistently.
2. Request demonstrations when the rule is ambiguous. One plausible interpretation is not enough; use examples to distinguish local motifs, propagation, symmetry, and global rules.
3. Infer transformations from input-output differences. Identify changed cells and color mappings, then test candidate rules against every demo. Prefer a compact rule explaining all examples over intuition-based motif extension.
4. Apply the verified rule mechanically to the test. Preserve unchanged cells and dimensions unless evidence says otherwise; account for boundaries and overlaps.
5. Before submitting, reproduce every demo output exactly using the candidate rule. Check dimensions, row lengths, legal colors, and boundary behavior. If any demo fails, refine the hypothesis or request another demo.
6. Follow the protocol exactly: one valid action JSON per turn, on the final line. Submit only a complete grid; request a demo when further evidence is worth its cost.

## Pitfalls
- A salient multi-cell object in the test may be an instruction, seed, or unrelated element, not the rule itself. Establish its role from examples.
- Never generalize a local neighborhood mapping to every marker without checking the complete demo output. Wrong submissions consume attempts.
- Keep reasoning separate from the required response format; when the task requires one action, provide only that action.

## Validation checklist
- Candidate rule reproduces every demo exactly.
- Test output has intended dimensions and legal integer colors.
- Original non-background cells are preserved or changed only as specified.
- Boundary clipping and overlapping transformations are handled consistently.
- Final response contains exactly one action object.

# ARC demonstration synthesis

Use when a puzzle allows costly demonstration requests and examples vary in grid size, color, or seed appearance.

## Workflow
1. For each pair, record background, all non-background coordinates, changed coordinates, color changes, and exact unchanged regions.
2. State what the new pair proves and compare it against every previous pair before requesting another demo or submitting.
3. Keep a small explicit hypothesis set. For band-like or sparse stripe seeds, distinguish partial-row extension to an edge, completion of an exceptional row in a repeated pattern, motif copying, and periodic-field completion. Treat unchanged counterpart rows/cells as negative evidence.
